chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from the one who mentioned it, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorces his wife, and between the two of them is a child, which of the two is more rightful with the child? He (peace be upon him) said: The woman is more rightful with the child so long as she does not marry (again).
ai.seo_question: Who has primary custody of young children after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default custody arrangement (hadanah) in Shia jurisprudence, affirming the mother's primary right to care for young children post-divorce. The condition of remarriage serves as the critical legal threshold for transferring custody, reflecting the principle that the mother's marital status impacts her ability to provide a stable domestic environment for the child.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Minqary, from the one who mentioned it, said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who divorces his wife, and between the two of them is a child, which of the two is more rightful with the child?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The woman is more rightful with the child so long as she does not get married (again)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasaniy from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Minqariy from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “

Once, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who divorces his wife. They have a child, which one of them has more right for the child? He (the Imam) said, ‘The woman has more right as long as she does not marry.’”
